In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new no-reference quality assessment (NRQA) model for high-dynamic-range (HDR) images.
the problem of how to automatically predict the subjective quality, as perceived in the human visual system (HVS), of HDR pictures.
the problem of automatically predicting the perceived quality of tone-mapped HDR pictures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed models and algorithms can effectively predict the subjective image quality of HDR pictures, even without a reference, and that these models are robust enough to predict the subjective quality not only of HDR pictures but also of SDR pictures.

the proposed NR IQA model and algorithm for HDR pictures outperforms the state of the art on both legacy natural SDR and crowdsourced HDR images, while being computationally efficient and easy to implement.
the proposed models are able to accurately predict the perceived quality of tone-mapped HDR images and that the models can be applied to SDR legacy natural images with high accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed NR IQA models for HDR pictures can predict the subjective quality better than the state-of-the-art NR IQA models designed for SDR images.

our proposed HDR-specific NR IQA model and algorithm are the first to achieve high correlation between the predicted and the actual subjective quality of HDR images, and are among the best-performing NR IQA algorithms for SDR images as well.
we have developed an effective NR IQA algorithm for tone-mapped HDR pictures that can be applied to any HDR picture without the need of a reference image.
